# Points of sail

The points of sail describe a boat's heading relative to the true wind. Close-hauled, beam reach, broad reach and running each ask for a different trim of the mainsail and jib. See [[Reading the wind]] before choosing a heading.

## Close-hauled

Sailing as close to the wind as the boat allows, about 45 degrees off it. Sheet the sails in hard and steer by the telltales on the jib luff.

## Running downwind

With the wind behind the boat, ease the mainsail all the way out and watch for an accidental gybe. A preventer line on the boom keeps it from slamming across.
